title: Candidate First 6-Week Success Canvas and Async Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This working canvas captures a candidate-centric 6-week activation plan aimed at maximizing early success for hires across IC, manager, and contractor roles. It is intentionally lightweight, asynchronous-first, and designed to be automatable where possible. Use as a baseline for role-specific adaptations.

Scope and intended outcomes:
- Scope: New full-time engineers, product managers, and contractor ICs joining engineering orgs. Excludes interns and executive hires (separate flows).
- Outcomes in 6 weeks: access provisioned, clear first-issue shipped or equivalent impact milestone defined, manager and buddy sync cadence established, candidate feels connected to team and mission, basic production access and safety training completed.
- Success metrics (sample): 80% of hires complete Week 1 checklist within 7 days; 70% hit their Week 4 milestone; < 3 open access/permission blockers by Day 10.

Owners and roles:
- People Ops (Priya Nair): owner of the template, automation sequences, and hiring manager nudges.
- Hiring Manager: responsible for role ramp plan, weekly 1:1s, and performance expectations.
- Buddy (peer): tactical first-week support and small-task pairing.
- IT/Security: accounts and access provisioning SLA (target 3 business days).

Preboarding (Offer accepted -> Day 0) — async checklist:
- Day 0 email sequence (auto):
  - T0: Offer acceptance confirmation + next steps link + onboarding calendar invite (hr@redwood.com).
  - T+2 (if no profile set): reminder to complete HR form + equipment preference.
  - T+5: send team intro note template w/ public Slack channels to join.
- HR tasks: send benefits doc, confirm payroll, tax forms.
- IT tasks: open equipment order ticket; create short-lived onboarding VPN creds; list external SaaS accounts to be granted.
- Hiring Manager tasks: create first-6-week impact milestone in team board (template: 3 tangible outcomes).

Day 0 / Week 0 (arrival):
- Quick wins to enable confidence:
  - Equip: laptop delivered or pickup confirmed; dev environment doc link.
  - Access: email, Slack, VPN, code host read access, CI status dashboard.
  - Intro: 30-min team welcome + 15-min buddy intro.
  - Security: complete mandatory security checklist (SAML enrollment, MFA).
- Manager: 30-min expectation-setting (role scope, where to find docs, first-issue assignment).

Week 1 — orientation and first pairing:
- Goals: baseline environment healthy; small pairing task; social orientation.
- Checklist:
  - Complete HR orientation recording and knowledge quiz.
  - Join recurring team standups and retro channel.
  - Run onboarding-runbook.sh and verify dev build passes locally.
  - Buddy: pair on first issue and PR review process.
  - Manager: set 1:1 cadence (weekly) and document 6-week plan in Confluence.
- People Ops nudges: Day 4 check-in email asking about blockers; escalate to manager if not resolved by Day 6.

Week 2 — ownership and small deliverable:
- Goals: complete first small deliverable (bugfix or doc), begin independent PRs.
- Checklist:
  - Create first PR and complete 1 cycle of review feedback.
  - Attend product/roadmap session to learn higher-level context.
  - Security & compliance micro-training completed (e-sign).

Week 3 — cadence and feedback loop:
- Goals: demonstrate independent contributions, first feedback loop.
- Checklist:
  - Manager conducts week-3 1:1 focused on ramp progress and blockers.
  - 360 feedback prompt sent to peers who worked with hire (async template).
  - People Ops: measure access issues and ping infra for any lingering tickets.

Week 4 — milestone checkpoint (midpoint):
- Goals: achieve or be on-track for the mid-6-week milestone; formal touchpoint.
- Checklist:
  - 6-week milestone status update posted to team board.
  - Manager completes a short mid-ramp rubric (see Interview + Onboard Rubric section).
  - People Ops triggers a short retention pulse survey (3 questions).

Week 5 — scale and depth:
- Goals: deeper system ownership, proactive suggestions for improvement.
- Checklist:
  - Hire leads a small design discussion or retrospective.
  - Manager documents next 90-day outcomes with clear success criteria.

Week 6 — closure and 6-week review:
- Goals: finalize first-6-week evaluation, calibrate ongoing support.
- Checklist:
  - Manager and hire complete 6-week review form; score against rubric.
  - If at-risk: create a 30-day remediation plan with People Ops.
  - Celebrate: team shoutout + highlight first contribution.

Interview + Onboard Rubric (compact) — use for mid-ramp and final 6-week review:
- Dimensions (score 1–4, 4=exceeds expectations):
  - Technical delivery: completes tasks, code quality, debug process.
  - Product sense: understands user impact and tradeoffs.
  - Collaboration: communicates clearly, responsive in reviews, gives/receives feedback.
  - Ownership & initiative: identifies gaps and proposes solutions.
  - Security & compliance posture: follows mandatory controls and risk practices.
- Quick calibration notes: 3s = on-track with some support; 2s = needs more synchronous onboarding; 1s = requires immediate remediation planning.

Hiring manager playbook (practical bullets):
- Before Day 0: add first-issue + 6-week milestone to tracker, pick a buddy, set 1:1 calendar recurring.
- Week 0–2: daily async check-ins via Slack for blockers, 30-min 1:1 in Week 1.
- Week 3–6: weekly 1:1s focused on outcomes, not status. Use the rubric during week 4 and week 6.
- When hire scores average <= 2 at week 4: escalate to People Ops and prepare remediation steps.

Candidate communication templates (short snippets to use in automation):
- Offer acceptance ack: "Welcome! Quick next steps: confirm start date, fill benefits form, schedule equipment pickup."
- Day 3 welcome (team intro): "Join #team-<slug> and say hi; your buddy is <name>. Here are 3 things to read before your first pair."
- Blocker escalation to manager: "Hi <manager>, new joiner <name> reported access blocker: <ticket>. Please advise."

Automation rules (People Ops playbook):
- Rule 1: If dev access not granted by Day 3 -> auto escalate to infra via ONBOARD-412 and notify hiring manager.
- Rule 2: If security quiz not completed by Day 7 -> weekly reminder up to 3x then manager alert.
- Rule 3: Send 3-question retention pulse at Week 4; if negative signal detected, open a People Ops review.

Open questions (items to iterate in this doc):
- Should managers be required to publish role-level 6-week milestones in a canonical org-level board? (tradeoff: overhead vs clarity)
- Best minimal training set for contractors with limited access?
- Tone calibration for automated emails to reduce noise for hiring managers.

Appendix: short templates and sample forms (copy/paste)
- Mid-ramp 3-question pulse (Week 4):
  1) How supported do you feel? (1-5)
  2) What is your biggest blocker right now? (free text)
  3) One thing we should do differently to help you ramp faster? (free text)
- Sample remediation micro-plan (30 days):
  - Focus areas: access, pairing schedule, targeted training items.
  - Measurable outcomes: 2 PRs merged, pass security quiz, reduce open tickets to 0.

Todo / next steps for this draft:
- [ ] Validate automation rules with infra and legal (Marcus Reed).
- [ ] Localize template wording for non-US hires (timezones & benefits).
- [ ] Build onboarding status dashboard (owner: analytics team).

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive where blocking work is common and intentionally lightweight where managers should retain discretion. Please comment on the 6-week milestone template and propose any role templates (SRE/Platform/PM) you want included.
